First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}=\frac{A}{(x+2)}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-3)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+2)^{2}(x-3)$ and get

$$
5x+35=A(x+2)(x-3)+B(x-3)+C(x+2)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-2)+35 & =A(-2+2)(-2-3)+B(-2-3)+C(-2+2)^{2} \\ -10+35 & =B(-5) \\ B & =\frac{25}{-5} \\ B & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(3)+35 & =A(3+2)(3-3)+B(3-3)+C(3+2)^{2} \\ 15+35 & =C{(5)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{50}{25} \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(0)+35 & =A(0+2)(0-3)+B(0-3)+C(0+2)^{2} \\ 35 & =-6A-3B+4C \\ 35 & =-6A-3(-5)+4(2) \\ 35 & =-6A+23 \\ 6A & =-35+23 \\ A & =\frac{-12}{6} \\ A & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}=-\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{5}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-3)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x+35}{(x+2)^{2}(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{2}{(x+2)}-\frac{5}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-3)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+\frac{5}{x+2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
